title: POC weekly sync - SDK function calls & structured output integration

Redwood to provide sample SDK snippet, validation schema, and pilot SOW; customer to run extended late-night load test and share telemetry.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20 14:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Acme CTO), Priya Patel (Lead ML Eng), Jorge Ramirez (PM)

Summary: quick sync on SDK function calling and structured output integration. a few blockers around schema validation and network access for Private.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick checkin, we're at 45 minutes, we'll do updates then action items. Maya, want to start with engineering status?
[00:18] Maya Singh: yeah sure uh thanks Alex. Priya, we saw the test logs you sent last night — overall looks good, the model responses are hitting the sdk tool call hook as expected. a couple of things: one is the JSON payload shape sometimes has a stray comma or missing field when the generator tries to be concise, and two is the retry path on 502s from the function endpoint.
[00:40] Priya Patel: yes, we noticed that. in our integration with the product inference service the structured output validator is our blocker. sometimes it returns an array where we expect an object, and the client-side json-schema check fails. could be prompt tuning but also maybe the function calling mapping is off.
[01:05] Jorge Ramirez: quick q — are we using the newer function-calling SDK or rolling our own post-processing?
[01:12] Maya Singh: you're on the Redwood SDK function-calling beta, right? we sent the snippet last week. it surfaces the tool call event and then you implement the tool handler. so the runtime returns a single canonical object: {tool_call: {name, arguments}} — though i think the transcript had a couple mislabels because of transcription.
[01:38] Liam O'Connor: i mean, it looks promising. Priya, does this block your E2E or is it just validation noise?
[01:44] Priya Patel: it's blocking automated ingestion, so yes until we have deterministic schema enforcement it fails our pipeline. we tested with 500 examples; about 6% had schema mismatches. some were obvious prompt-edge cases.
[02:10] Maya Singh: ok 6% is in the range we've seen when structured output isn't constrained. options: we can push more constrained system prompts, or use Redwood's structured-output validation layer in the SDK which will coerce/raise errors. we have a sample validator that returns a normalized object and a list of issues.
[02:40] Alex Chen: and that validator can be toggled to "coerce" mode so non-fatal issues get fixed automatically, or strict mode so it fails loudly. for pilot you might want strict mode to capture edge cases, then switch to coerce for production.
[02:55] Priya Patel: can you share the sample? we tried to implement something locally but could be different.
[03:02] Maya Singh: yes i'll post a gist and an inline snippet. the gist includes retries with exponential backoff for function postbacks and how to wire the sdk callback to your microservice.
[03:20] Jorge Ramirez: on the function calling side, we saw a few 502s during spikes — is Redwood handling retries or should our handler be idempotent and retry?
[03:30] Maya Singh: the SDK has a default retry for transient errors when invoking external tools, but it's intended that your handler be idempotent. we also support async callbacks: if your tool needs more time, you can return a 202 with a callback URL and Redwood will poll.
[03:52] Liam O'Connor: that async callback feature is good for our long-running matches. is there documentation for the callback flow?
[03:58] Alex Chen: yes there's a section in the integration guide. i'll link it in the follow-up.
[04:10] Priya Patel: networking question — for the Private deployment we need to know whether to expect VPC peering or full Private control plane. our security team prefers peering + egress controls.
[04:22] Liam O'Connor: plus we need KMS integration for PHI at rest. are we ok on that?
[04:30] Maya Singh: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we offer envelope encryption but not customer KMS. for Private, we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and we surface key rotation logs in the audit trail.
[04:44] Priya Patel: can you provide the KMS integration doc and SOC 2 summary?
[04:48] Alex Chen: yes, we'll attach the SOC 2 summary and a KMS integration checklist in the follow-up.
[05:00] Jorge Ramirez: coming back to output schema — some of the mismatches were subtle: e.g., numbers encoded as strings, optional fields missing entirely. could the SDK do type coercion?
[05:12] Maya Singh: the validator has rules for type coercion. there's a mode where it will coerce strings to numbers based on the schema with a warning, or reject. we can also emit a per-inference diagnostics blob that you can send to your QA pipeline.
[05:28] Priya Patel: that diagnostics blob would be super helpful. where does that sit in terms of PII? does it contain raw prompts or redacted?
[05:36] Maya Singh: by default we redact user identifiers in diagnostics, but you can opt-in to include full prompts for debugging if your security policy allows it. for Private deployment you can store diagnostics in your own S3 or object store behind your VPC.
[05:52] Liam O'Connor: ok that sounds workable. next, latency: we ran a small perf test — median token latency was ok but tail spiked under concurrency. any advice on batching or streaming to reduce cost?
[06:08] Maya Singh: so batching reduces per-token cost but increases latency. for interactive UI flows we recommend small batch sizes and streaming so you can render partial tokens. for background jobs, larger batches are better. Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching and automatic KV cache reuse which helps with repeated prefixes.
[06:30] Jorge Ramirez: are there config knobs we can set per-route? we want one route for chat UI and another for nightly bulk scoring.
[06:36] Maya Singh: yes you can define route configs with batch windows, max batch size, and latency SLOs. you can also pin those routes to Dedicated capacity if you want predictable throughput.
[06:48] Priya Patel: for the pilot we are on hosted but would prefer Dedicated if we see stable throughput. what is the threshold for that conversation?
[06:56] Alex Chen: typically customers start conversation after sustained monthly usage above 1-2M tokens or when they need isolated capacity or SLA guarantees. we can run benchmarks on Dedicated but usually that's a sales conversation.
[07:12] Priya Patel: noted. back to SDK specifics — we had an integration bug where the SDK's streaming chunk had an extra newline and our parser crashed. is that a known issue?
[07:24] Maya Singh: there was a prior edge-case in older SDK versions where streaming boundaries could include trailing whitespace. which SDK version are you using?
[07:32] Priya Patel: 0.9.1-beta.
[07:36] Maya Singh: ok please upgrade to 0.9.3, that fixes whitespace trimming and a more robust chunk assembler. we'll include a migration note.
[07:48] Alex Chen: i'll put that in the follow-up too.
[07:54] Jorge Ramirez: any tips for testing function-call idempotency?
[07:58] Maya Singh: best practice is attach a request-id and have your handler detect duplicates. the SDK will retry on network errors so design idempotent handlers or use unique invocation ids. we have a snippet demonstrating an idempotency key in the gist.
[08:18] Priya Patel: about monitoring — can we get token-level cost insights per route? our finance wants to track pilot burn.
[08:26] Alex Chen: yes Redwood Console gives per-route token breakdown, top prompts, and cost estimates. we can give you pilot access to the console.
[08:36] Liam O'Connor: security again — audit logs and RBAC, can we lock down which teams can call certain routes?
[08:44] Maya Singh: yes RBAC integrates with SSO and you can scope API keys to specific routes and rate limits. for Private deployments you can also enforce network-based access.
[08:55] Priya Patel: thanks. one more integration detail: when the model triggers a tool call and expects structured JSON back from our tool, what validation should we do before returning the result back to Redwood for finalization?
[09:08] Maya Singh: validate against the same schema you expect the model to produce. our recommended flow: validate incoming model arguments, run the tool, validate tool output, then return a canonical object to the SDK. if validation fails, return a structured error so Redwood can prompt the model for clarification.
[09:28] Jorge Ramirez: can Redwood synthesize clarifying prompts automatically on validation failure?
[09:32] Maya Singh: there's a built-in fallback policy that can attempt up to N clarification retries with templated prompts. you control the policy per-route.
[09:44] Alex Chen: also worth noting — you can run a canary rollout where 10% of traffic goes to a tighter validation policy and 90% to lax to measure impact.
[09:56] Priya Patel: good to know.
[10:00] Liam O'Connor: about the 6% mismatch, can Redwood run a batch eval and produce a report of common failure modes?
[10:08] Maya Singh: yep we have Redwood Optimize evals — we can run a small batch and return a report with top prompt failure buckets and suggested prompt patches.
[10:20] Priya Patel: please do, that'll help prioritize fixes.
[10:24] Alex Chen: action item: we'll run a 1k-sample eval and share the Optimize report.
[10:30] Jorge Ramirez: quick question on telemetry sharing — can we upload logs to your console or should we host and give you a link?
[10:38] Maya Singh: for Private, we prefer you host and give us read-only links. for hosted pilot you can upload to the console; we redact PII by default.
[10:48] Priya Patel: we'll host in our S3 and give you presigned links.
[10:52] Alex Chen: perfect. 
[10:56] Priya Patel: one last thing — the product team wants structured output to include provenance for each field (which prompt generated it, confidence score). is that supported?
[11:06] Maya Singh: yes the SDK can attach metadata fields per inference: confidence estimates, provenance, and tokens used. the structured object can include a _meta section that your pipeline can parse.
[11:18] Jorge Ramirez: will that increase token usage?
[11:20] Maya Singh: minimal — metadata is appended but small; for strict cost control you can toggle how much metadata we include.
[11:28] Alex Chen: okay we're at the 20-minute mark in the transcript here, happy to speed through the remaining items.
[11:34] Liam O'Connor: quick scheduling note: we'd like a performance demo with Dedicated next Wed.
[11:40] Alex Chen: i'll check availability and propose times.
[11:44] Priya Patel: also can you include a snippet showing schema validation failure handling so our frontend can surface errors to QA?
[11:52] Maya Singh: yes we'll include that in the gist.
[12:00] Jorge Ramirez: are there any known limits on function call payload size? sometimes our tool returns large JSONs.
[12:08] Maya Singh: payloads > 1MB should be avoided; for large outputs return a pointer (S3 link) and Redwood will fetch or proxy it depending on config.
[12:20] Priya Patel: ok we'll adapt.
[12:24] Alex Chen: any other blockers from your side?
[12:28] Priya Patel: mainly the schema mismatches and a final decision on Private vs hosted for pilot.
[12:34] Liam O'Connor: security has minor questions but nothing blocking.
[12:38] Alex Chen: final recap: Redwood to send SOW and pricing, SOC 2 and KMS notes, SDK gist with function-calling + validation + retry patterns, and we'll run a 1k eval. Acme to run extended load test, confirm networking preference, and share telemetry links.
[12:58] Jorge Ramirez: sounds good. thanks all.
[13:02] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and the action item list.

Notes on transcription quality: some proper nouns mis-transcribed; code references are paraphrased.
